$comment: Hand-written answers for the grader's unit test (test/scripts/evals.test.mjs): per case, a good answer that must pass and a bad one that must fail for the reasons named in `fails`. Triage answers are parsed reports; the others are Markdown.

good.summary: Several services fail and one host probes a server.

findings.title: Port scan from 10.0.0.66
findings.detail: 10.0.0.66 connected to 10.0.0.80 on ports 22, 23, 445, 3389 and 5900, which looks like reconnaissance.

findings.title: Connections reset
findings.detail: Five TCP resets: the probed ports refused the connections.

findings.title: HTTP 503 Service Unavailable
findings.detail: The web server answered four requests with 503.

findings.title: DNS errors
findings.detail: Three NXDOMAIN answers and one query without a response.

findings.title: Unanswered pings
findings.detail: Three ICMP echo requests got no reply.

bad.summary: The network looks mostly fine. There are no clear-text credentials.

findings.title: TLS handshake failures
findings.detail: Some TLS sessions ended with an alert.

good.summary: No significant problems: every connection was accepted and every DNS query answered.

findings.title: Normal office traffic
findings.detail: HTTP and DNS between the workstations and the servers, nothing reset or retransmitted.

findings.title: Retransmissions
findings.detail: Some segments were retransmitted, which suggests congestion.

good.summary: Mostly healthy services with three small errors.

findings.title: HTTP 404 Not Found
findings.detail: One request asked for a page the server doesn't have.

findings.title: DNS error answer
findings.detail: One query was answered with No such name.

findings.title: Unanswered ping
findings.detail: One ICMP echo request got no reply.

bad.summary: A host appears to scan the network.

findings.title: Port scan
findings.detail: The SNMP manager scans several hosts.

good.summary: Passwords cross the network in clear text.

findings.title: Clear-text credentials
findings.detail: HTTP Basic, FTP, POP3 and IMAP logins send user names and passwords unencrypted.

findings.title: Connection resets
findings.detail: The FTP server reset the session.

office-summary.good:
## Overview

An office network: workstations talk HTTP to 10.0.0.80 and DNS to 10.0.0.53.

## Problems

- 10.0.0.66 contacts 10.0.0.80 on many ports (22, 23, 445, 3389, 5900), which looks like a port scan.
- Five connections were reset (RST): the probed ports refused them.
- The web server answered four requests with HTTP 503 Service Unavailable.
- DNS errors: three NXDOMAIN answers.

Nothing suggests credentials were exposed.
office-summary.bad:
## Overview

An office network with HTTP and DNS traffic.

- Some TLS handshake errors appear between the clients and the web server.
- Traffic volume is steady.

office-compare.good:
## What changed

- **A new host, 10.0.0.66**, connects to 10.0.0.80 on ports 22, 23, 445, 3389 and 5900: a port scan that wasn't there before.
- **Resets**: 0 → 5 per capture; the scanned ports refused the connections.
- **HTTP 5xx**: the web server now answers four requests with 503.
- **DNS**: three NXDOMAIN errors and one unanswered query, none before.
- **ICMP**: three echo requests got no reply.

No host or service disappeared.
office-compare.bad:
## What changed

The traffic is about the same. The DNS server disappeared from the later capture, and the file server is gone.

New services being accessed: 10.0.0.66 connects to 10.0.0.80 on ports 22, 23, 445, 3389 and 5900.
